title: Thompson v. South Florida Presbytery
disposition_detail: SJC found the BCO 40-5 application administratively out of order and not capable of being put in order under OMSJC 9.1.a.; it dismissed the case under OMSJC 9.2(d) because BCO 40-3 bars review and control of proceedings in a judicial case once notice of appeal or complaint has been given the lower court.
first_summary: The SJC dismissed John Thompson's BCO 40-5 application against South Florida Presbytery because BCO 40-3 bars review and control of proceedings in a judicial case after notice of appeal or complaint is given the lower court.
summary: The SJC dismissed a BCO 40-5 application because the matter concerned proceedings in a judicial case in which a complaint had been filed. Under BCO 40-3, such proceedings may not be handled by review and control once notice of appeal or complaint is given to the lower court. The SJC therefore found the case administratively out of order and not capable of being put in order under OMSJC 9.1.a., and dismissed it under OMSJC 9.2(d).
